# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for CPU builds
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, MPI, and other LAMMPS dependencies
# Also installs ca-certificates, libgomp1, and python3 as required
# FIX: Added python3 to satisfy the LAMMPS build system dependency.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    ca-certificates \
    python3 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code, build it, and clean up
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps-src && \
    cd /opt/lammps-src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with the required REAXFF package and MPI support
    cmake ../cmake \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
      -D BUILD_MPI=on \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && \
    # Build LAMMPS using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the compiled executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Create the final working directory
    mkdir -p /app && \
    # Copy the required example files into the working directory
    cp /opt/lammps-src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size
    rm -rf /opt/lammps-src

# Set the working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# The container is now ready. The 'lmp' executable is on the PATH.
# To run an MPI job, use a command like:
# mpirun -np <num_procs> --allow-run-as-root --mca btl_tcp_if_exclude lo,docker0 lmp -in <your_input_script>
# Setting a default command to an interactive shell for ease of use.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS experiment
# on a single AWS CPU-based Kubernetes node using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-hns
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size of the MiniCluster, corresponding to the number of pods.
  # Set to 1 to satisfy the "run on only one node" requirement.
  size: 1

  # The launcher container is typically used to submit jobs to the Flux broker.
  # By setting this to false, we indicate that this container is part of the main workload.
  launcher: false

  # Logging mode: 'strict' will fail the job on any error encountered.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Job cleanup policy. False preserves pods after completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the single container that will run the LAMMPS simulation.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed within the container.
      # The Flux Operator will automatically wrap this command with `flux run`.
      # The command runs the LAMMPS executable `lmp` with the specified input file and variables.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

# This is a corrected MiniCluster manifest to run a LAMMPS experiment.
# The primary fix is moving the 'launcher' field from the top-level spec
# to its correct location within the container definition, resolving the
# 'unknown field "spec.launcher"' schema error. This version adheres
# strictly to the original constraints, avoiding any unspecified
# optimizations or node-specific configurations.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reax-hns
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1

  # Logging mode: 'strict' will fail the job on any error encountered.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Job cleanup policy: false preserves pods and logs after completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the single container that will run the LAMMPS simulation.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed. The Flux Operator will wrap this in `flux run`.
      # Using the exact command as originally requested.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # CORRECTED: The 'launcher' field belongs inside the container definition.
      # It indicates this container is part of the main workload.
      launcher: false

# This manifest fixes the previous execution error by setting 'launcher: true'.
# When launcher is true, the Flux Operator wraps the container's command
# with 'flux run', enabling the command to execute in parallel across
# the 64 tasks specified. The previous setting 'launcher: false' caused the
# command to run as a single, non-parallel process.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-hns
  namespace: default
spec:
  # This job will run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Total MPI tasks to run for the job.
  tasks: 64
  # Do not delete pods after the job finishes for inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Set logging to fail the job on any error.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings required for running on an ARM-based node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod specification to control scheduling.
  pod:
    # Schedule the pod onto a specific high-performance instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Application container definition.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    # CORRECTED: This must be true to have the Flux Operator use 'flux run'
    # to launch the command in parallel across the specified tasks.
    launcher: true
    # The command is optimized for a 64-task run (4x4x4 decomposition).
    command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
